title: finding(tooling): `field:owner` is registered at runtime and missing from the generated universe — the indirect bypass is keyed by FILE while the table's coverage is keyed by COLLECTION
body:
Dedup keywords: `indirect bypass file-scoped` · `RETIRED_FIELD_TYPES` · `registerAllFields` tombstone · missing registry key · `deriveRegistryKeys`

Surfaced by the `os-dev` delivering objectui#9703 (PR objectui#9716) and **re-verified on `origin/main` by the `domain:spec` @ objectui execution seat before filing**. ⛔ Filed as a `finding`; grading, `domain:*` and routing are the triage seat's.

⚠️ This is **not** the escalation objectui#9703's triage condition named. That condition was a namespace *disagreement* among the hand-kept table's entries, and it did **not** fire — the dev measured 245/245 agree with both mutation controls lit. This is a different defect: a **missing** key.

## The reading

`field:owner` is registered at runtime by `registerAllFields()` — the `RETIRED_FIELD_TYPES` tombstone loop, namespace `field`, `skipFallback: true` — and is **absent** from the derived key universe **and** from `packages/cli/src/utils/known-schema-types.ts`.

| probe on `origin/main` | reading |
|---|---|
| `'field:owner'` in `known-schema-types.ts` | **0** |
| **lit control** `'field:user'` | 1 |
| **lit control** `'protocol-placeholder:view:grid'` | 1 |
| **absent control** `'field:zzznosuch'` | 0 |

⇒ both controls fire, so the zero is a reading.

`RETIRED_FIELD_TYPES` itself (`packages/core/src/utils/retired-field-types.ts`) declares **exactly one** key, `owner`, and its own message ends: *"The `widget: 'field:owner'` spelling is retired with it."*

## The mechanism

```
scripts/check-doc-component-types.mjs:1394
  const indirectSites = new Set(indirect.map((entry) => entry.site));
scripts/check-doc-component-types.mjs:1429
  if (indirectSites.has(rel)) { … }
```

The indirect bypass is keyed by **FILE**, while the hand-kept table's coverage is keyed by **COLLECTION**. ⇒ **any** unresolvable registration living in a table-named file is skipped silently — including one whose collection the table never names. The bypass was built to skip the entries the table covers; it also skips everything else in the same file.

## ⛔ Why this was reported and not repaired, which is the interesting part

Surfacing that call turns it into an `unresolved-registration` finding — but **whether a retired tombstone spelling belongs in a universe whose job is "does this string name a component that exists" is a judgement, not a mechanic.**

⭐ A document teaching `field:owner` arguably **should** go red. Today it does — but **by accident**, through a file-keyed bypass that was never reasoned about for this case rather than through any decision that retired spellings stay out. The behaviour may well be correct; the mechanism producing it is not one anybody chose.

⇒ that is why the bounded in-place fix conditions fail on "mechanical", and why the dev stopped and reported. ⛔ This seat agrees and did not repair it either.

## What this card asks for

1. Decide whether retired tombstone spellings belong in the derived universe at all.
2. Whichever way that goes, decide whether the bypass should be keyed by collection rather than by file — because today the right answer for `field:owner` is produced by a mechanism that would give the *wrong* answer for any non-retired registration that happened to share a file with a table-named collection.

⚠️ Note for whoever takes it: PR objectui#9716 (card objectui#9703) rewrites the namespace derivation in this same file. ⛔ Do not start this card against a stale reading of `check-doc-component-types.mjs` — re-derive against `main` after that PR lands.
